drafted_from: tool:picture-an-app-window row in tools/look-at-screen/tool-rows.json, do-work/look-at-screen.mjs (lookAtWindow), read-data/rules.json and test/look-at-screen.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Show me what the Notes window looks like right now." It runs tool:picture-an-app-window once with owner_name "Notes" and describes the picture.
no_lists_because: It names no list: it takes a picture only when run, keeps nothing on the Mac and answers the picture in its reply.
instructions: 1. Allow Screen Recording for the app that runs the tool in System Settings, Privacy & Security; without it the tool answers needs_access and captures nothing.

2. Say which app; your AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run and tool tool:picture-an-app-window, with owner_name (the app's name as this Mac lists it) and long_edge (200 to 1600 pixels) if you want a smaller picture.
3. Read the answer: picture has width and height in pixels, media_type image/jpeg and base64 bytes; window has the window's id and title.
4. If the answer says no_window, the app has no window on screen: open one and ask again. Nothing is clicked or raised either way.

worked_examples.title: One app's front window, smaller picture
worked_examples.ask: Picture the Mail window, 500 pixels on the long side.
worked_examples.given: From tools/look-at-screen/test/look-at-screen.test.mjs (system commands stood in for): Mail lists one ordinary window, id 3, titled Inbox; Screen Recording is allowed. Read from do-work/look-at-screen.mjs: long_edge 500 is under the rules' limit so it is used, and only window 3 is captured.
worked_examples.hands_back: window {id 3, name "Inbox", owner "Mail"}, picture {width, height (as the shrink step reports them), media_type "image/jpeg", base64 ...}, said "This is the app's frontmost window as it is on the screen now; the picture gives its size in pixels." and looked_at a time. For an app with no window on screen it answers {no_window: "Mail", said: "That app has no window on the screen now. Open it, or bring one of its windows back from the Dock, and ask again."}.
